verdictReasons.changedArea: Four of the five changed tracks hold, and three of them are demonstrably better than the live build. The changed area still fails on three counts. (1) A regression this build introduced: commit 67e0a41 made the FFX results ledger derive its ROW SET from AP eligibility, so a member who fought and is KO'd at the end vanishes from the results screen and a defeat shows no member rows at all (PR-0003, independently confirmed). (2) Its own claimed fix does not hold where it matters: the strategy guide still slices its last line and prints the MORE chip over its own text, at 1600x900 and at Bailey's 2000x1012 (PR-0009). (3) The engine track's own new subsystem leaves a sourced rule unimplemented at runtime: a Threatened enemy still counterattacks, because the canCounter guard that encodes the rule has no call site (PR-0004). Separately, three of the four changed engine subsystems are still not proved to run through the real presentation path (CHK-023 UNVERIFIED), and the 'mute is applied at boot' claim is wider than the code.

Unchanged high-risk sampling: all 19 ICV_BASE breakpoints and their predecessors match 1.2, 17 sampled command ranks match 1.3, and FFX-2's ATB runs at 3,000 ticks/s (303,964 ticks over 101,321 ms, measured live). HELD DOWN BY: a major, sourced, runtime-observed defect in the very subsystem this build rewrote - a Threatened enemy still counterattacks twice in one run, because the canCounter guard that encodes 'cannot act or counterattack' has no call site anywhere (PR-0004); the FFX-2 command fix filtering by category rather than by identity, which is latently over-broad (PR-0024); an unsourced rank-3 recovery constant carrying a citation that does not state it, plus a results.ts citation pointing at 1.7 for a 10.1 rule (PR-0025); and CHK-023 UNVERIFIED for three of the four changed engine subsystems, because no browser run has invoked Yu Yevon's counter guard, Gravija, or a denied sleeper turn.
